memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Obey these instructions as a lasting ordinance for you and your descendants.
When you enter the land that the LORD will give you as he promised, observe this
ceremony. And when your children ask you, 'What does this ceremony mean to you?'
then tell them, 'It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the
houses of the Israelites in Egypt and spared our homes when he struck down the
Egyptians.'" - Ex 12:24-27a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God plans for the questions of children. He anticipates a day, years ahead, when
a child watches the family prepare this meal and asks, "What does this mean?"

Notice that God does not tell the parents to give a lecture. He tells them to
tell the story. What God did. Where we were. How He spared us.

This is how faith travels between generations. Not primarily through argument or
instruction, but through parents who can say, honestly and simply, "Let me tell
you what God has done for us."

Notice also that the ceremony itself creates the question. The child asks because
something visible is happening. If nothing distinctive ever happens in a home,
children have nothing to ask about. Practices matter. A family that prays
together, opens Scripture, gives thanks at meals, keeps the Lord's Day, is
building things children will ask about.

Deuteronomy 6:7 says to talk of these things when you sit at home and when you
walk along the road. Ordinary moments. Ordinary conversation.

You do not need a theology degree to pass on faith. You need a story and a
willingness to tell it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God done in your life that you have never told your family?
2. Is there anything in your home that would make a child ask a question?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to live in such a way that those around me ask what it means. Give
me courage to tell them simply what You have done. Amen.
